Just tried on my pair of AP5 and had a walk around the house as too late to run in them. Initial impression is an improvement over the 4s in terms of a little more wiggle room in the toes and less of a taper into the little toe. 

They definitely feel more stable, little to no rolling out and there’s a lovely smooth transition from mid into forefoot. The lightstrike pro feels like it has more return but would need to run in them to truly confirm that.

Happy about the 4mm drop as that’s Goldilocks for me and they feel really light, not that the 4s were heavy, but these feel Metaspeed Sky/Edge light.

all_segments.text: Hey people, it's your midsole man Ed Budd here, back with another episode of the viewer favourite
running shoe, yay or nay. This is a series where I check out some soon-to-be-released or recently
released running shoes and let you know if I'm going to pick up a pair of them for review on
the channel or not. It's not me saying that the shoes are total fire or total trash, I'm not like
reviewing the shoes, it could be that I feel that some other shoe tubers might do them more justice
with a review. Some pairs though are just absolute must-buys and I have to review them here.
Four shoes to check out today and they include the Alphafly 4 from Nike which had a shock drop
very recently in a small supply. We've also got the Adidas Adios Pro 5 finally. We've got a shoe from
Ultra which is the Ultra Vanish Carbon 3 and last but not least the Puma Forever Un-Nitro 3.
You can go by for months without any new super shoes dropping and then you get like two in a week,
it's crazy. We finally have the Solar Turbo Core Black and Lucid Red version of the Adios Pro 5
appearing. It's in the shops now in fact £220 at retail. I was quite stunned to see that price.
There's lots of other models that are way, way over that. Adidas really keeping things very competitive
here with this pricing. We've got the typical midsole heel stack here around about 40mm. Very similar
light lock feature in the upper as well as per the previous version of the Adios Pro. Serrated laces too,
that's always a bonus to have and some people are suggesting this could be a new version of Light
Strike Pro. I'd be very surprised to see that we had the older version which we found in the Adios Pro 3
in the Evo SL as well. We then had what appeared to be a combination of different Light Strike Pro
materials in the Adios Pro 4 that were much softer. I think it'll probably still be like that although
it does appear that some people have various different versions of the Adios Pro 4 and they
all feel a little bit different. I would be very surprised to see it being a new formulation of
Light Strike Pro here. Now the big improvement here appears to be in the weight for the sample size
only 150 grams. That's about an ounce lighter than the Adios Pro 4. I think some of that weight saving
might be down to the new upper materials and of course the fact that we now have this energy rim
rather than those energy rods. So perhaps a little bit less of that carbon material or fiberglass or
whatever the hell it is. I've lost track of how many people have asked me about when this shoe comes
out so thank goodness it's finally here. I grabbed a pair after about a minute of them being available
because it's one of those shoes that I've always enjoyed testing out. Always had some really nice
memories of testing and racing in the Adios Pro series and I think it might be the same for this
one. So it's a big yay for the Adios Pro 5 from Adidas. Another race shoe here from Ultra. So apparently
this one only goes between a UK 7 and a UK 11. Not sure what's going on there. It's quite strange.
The Ultra Vanish Carbon 3 retails for the same price as the Adidas shoe $219.99. Though it is a much more
bulky shoe than the Adios Pro 5. I mean it really does make me quite excited about the Adios Pro 5 now
with that weight. There's a bit more rubber underfoot here and very little exposed midsole on that outsole
area. Of course we've got the typical expanded and extended toe box area here as you would expect
within an Ultra shoe allowing the toes to splay out a little bit more. Another key feature of this shoe
from Ultra is the fact it's only a 4mm drop. Now I tend to quite like lower drop shoes but when I saw
that this shoe is 220 grams for the sample size it really does strike home how light that Adidas shoe
is going to be. Like 70 grams lighter. That is insane. This one appears to use a two-piece
super critical Peeba midsole and it makes one of Ultra's lighter more responsive foams. Could be
perhaps more useful considering that outsole design if you're perhaps doing some sort of road to trail
race event. Maybe like an Ultra event even where you're on loads of different types of surfaces.
You're going between that road, loose debris like gravel and stuff so this could be fantastic for that.
I've got a boatload of like very cushioned carbon race shoes at the moment in the collection that are
all a bit lighter than this and I've always found that Ultra's fit might work really well for some
people but I've got a slightly narrow foot and it's always just way too baggy for me. So I think another
YouTuber will perhaps do a better more focused review on this one perhaps if they've got a slightly different
foot type. So for me it's a nay at the moment on the Ultra Vanish Carbon 3. A quick one now. I know that
a few pairs of the AlphaFly 4s have got out there to a few reviewers and I don't normally look at loads
of other shoe reviewers stuff like their content. I just don't have time. Sometimes though it's a bit
of a godsend to look at those reviews because you temper your expectation a little bit of something and it
does look like the AlphaFly 4 perhaps isn't the massive departure that it's made out to be. I mean
you can't make the AlphaFly all that much lighter due to its design. It is what it is. You've got to
have that slightly wider base. You've got to have the ZoomX foam. You've got to have the AirPods. You can
only take so much away from that before it isn't what the original design was or intended. The plastic
part of the pods, the surface area, the knit like upper are what makes the AlphaFly what it is. Take
it away and what are you left with. That's kind of the unique selling point to the shoe. I think 4D runs
has already confirmed. It's still loud and it squeaks. Chris you've got to get your WD40 out. A few squirts
in there. I've had to do that on all my AlphaFly's over the years. It does work. I'm not kidding. Are people
even bothered about the update here from the AF3? I mean you've got incredible deals on those right
now. Is this really needed? I've tested all three so far though so it kind of feels like a missed
opportunity not to test this new one out especially considering it's cheaper. But I mean Joker's already
out there trying to resell pairs of these over at StockX for £600. I mean you've got to be insane.
You've got to be clinically insane to think that it's worth that. I think maybe years ago perhaps
people would have done that but not now. If I get the opportunity to get a pair at retail when they
release I think I might pick up a pair just to see what it's like. But I don't think it's going to set
the world on fire. Let me know in the comments you know do you want to see an AlphaFly 4 review?
Do you care that much? It might be that no you don't. Last one up for me today is from Puma. This is the
Forever Run Nitro 3. This is one that's kind of bypassed me a little bit. I did enjoy the last
couple of versions of the shoe but found them to be a bit niche really. There's a hint of stability
there and I just found that the Velocity Nitro and also the Deviate Pure Nitro are stable enough for me.
Perhaps don't need the extra stability nods here. There's extra weight to the shoe. I think it's about
290 grams for the sample size so it's going to be well up into like the 330-340 mark for me which is
quite a chunky shoe. There's not a whole lot of difference here between the versions what I can see.
Similar outsole design as per the V1 and 2. They're still utilizing the power tape across the upper to
provide some extra structure. If you do overpronate then perhaps this could be a great model for you to
try out. It's a reasonable price as well around about 140 earth credits here in the UK. Does sound like
they're using a slightly firmer version of the Nitro foam here in the Forever Run in certain areas
just to you know enhance the support. Again if you overpronate could be a good option. Still provides a
big midsole stack there 38mm in the heel 30 up front for that 8mm drop. Just checking out the stats
there it does appear that it's a dual density construction which normally meant with this shoe
that it was a firmer sort of outer layer and then a softer inner layer. But for me I think it's one
of those niche options that I don't sort of grab for all that often. So it's a nay or new Forever Run
Nitro 3. I think I'd rather just run in the Deviate Pure Nitro or the Velocity Nitro. I'd perhaps benefit
more from less weight there. I just don't need the stability. Okay that's all the shoes in today's
yay or nay. Let me know your thoughts and opinions on all four of these down in the comments.
Quick musical interlude for you. While I was out running the Shoreditch Half Marathon the other day
a track came on the headphones which is always a favorite of mine. Kind of forgotten about it a
little bit but now I've been listening to it almost every day which is from Dillinger. It's called Acid Track.
One of his fantastic tunes from the 90s. What I loved about Dillinger's sound was the fact it was so
earthy and raw and real. You don't really get that these days with the overuse of computers.
Dillinger clearly using some sort of hardware sampler and lots of analog outboard gear to
really get this wonderful grimy sound. The distortion on that old outboard gear is just
way better than any sort of modelled stuff that you get. There's just this life to it. Even the way that
the sounds were triggered all feel a little bit more natural I suppose. It's one of the best
jungle drum and bass tracks ever in my opinion. Acid track. Go and check it out. Incredible propulsion,
loads of beat changes as well and some of the best bass sounds that you're ever going to hear. Thanks
for tuning in people. Hope you enjoyed today's video. Don't worry I've got lots of reviews coming up for you.
The Pegasus Plus 2 actually which I'm really enjoying so far. I know that some people got a bit of a
negative view on them but they're doing the business for me. That'll be coming up very soon
and I've got a pair of the Adios Pro 5s incoming too so very excited to try those out. Hit that
subscribe button if you're yet to do so. Give this video a thumbs up like and drop us a comment for the
algorithm. My name's Ed Budd and I'll be seeing you.
